chapter: Tatum, Wiggins and Los Angeles friends
title: Paul Chang and island pride in heritage
summary: He supplies the missing alto player's name, Paul Chang, and compares Barbados with Hawaii.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: One thing we could get in here now is, when we were playing...we'll do it over again... At the time we recorded originally, you couldn't remember the name of your other saxophone player in Honolulu.

It was Paul Chang. So I really had an international band. Paul Chang was full Chinese, the drummer was full Hawaiian, my tenor player was Hawaiian-Chinese, the piano player was Filipino-Chinese-Hawaiian.

And the funny thing about the Islands, everybody is proud of their heritage. They can tell you every branch of their family, and I can almost, too. For instance, my family came from Barbados, but... Did I have this before? Maybe.
We did it on Reel One.
Yes, so no point in going over that again. But Barbados is a great deal like Honolulu or the Islands, because it's in the same temperate zone and the climate is

just about the same, only Barbados still is untouched by a lot of crime, like Hawaii is. Barbados is a small island, 14 by 21, with 200,000 people, and the literacy rate is 98 percent. I'm proud of that.
So could I come back again?
